answer: Proof-of-stake serves as a robust inlet for Sybil resistance, requiring agents to lock capital to earn influence. An attacker aiming to simulate a reef of distinct nodes must commit significant financial marble to acquire stake, making the generation of infinite identities prohibitively expensive. This economic friction ensures that identity remains tied to scarce assets rather than computational volume, forcing adversaries to weigh the cost of capital against the negligible returns of malicious influence.
